My favorite transcription tool for Mac, MacWhisper, today received a major update adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, and a brand new transcription model. Details below.

MacWhisper 與 Apple Intelligence 整合更深入

I have written in the past about how heavily I rely on MacWhisper, especially as part of my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first AI-powered transcription tools for the Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it in 2023, it has continuously improved and expanded support for new models, services, and workflows.

These include automatic meeting recording, speaker identification, folder watching, system-wide input methods, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services such as Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today MacWhisper is releasing version 15.2, introducing improved speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was announced just hours ago.

This brings us to another major new feature in this update: live meeting transcription.

This feature has been near the top of MacWhisper's public roadmap for a long time, and it has finally arrived — users can now read along in real time during meetings, as well as search, copy, or send the live transcript.

As for the actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, which supports 22 languages, along with deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Users running macOS now (including those in the European Union) can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, pull text into Shortcuts, and reference on-screen transcripts in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organizing transcripts and meetings, with support for dragging existing transcription files in from the sidebar.
